subject: gk
question: The Ryotwari system, devised by Thomas Munro, in which peasant cultivators had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, was prevalent in which of the following present-day states/provinces?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ryotwari system was introduced in Tamil Nadu** during the British colonial period, primarily by the East India Company in the early 19th century.
 
• It was designed by **Sir Thomas Munro**, who was the Governor of Madras (now Chennai).
 
• The Ryotwari system involved **direct revenue collection from the cultivators.**
 
• The** tax rate was usually set at 50%** of the gross produce, but it could vary depending on the crop and local conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Ryotwari system was introduced in Odisha** during the British rule in the l**ate 19th century, particularly after the Famine of 1866.**
 
• The revenue rates were usually set at around** 25% to 50%** of the estimated yield, depending on the crop type and environmental factors.
 
• The **Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956,** later formalized revenue collection practices and land rights.
 
• **The Ryotwari system was implemented in Punjab** during the British colonial period, particularly **after the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-1846).**
 
• The **revenue rates **in Punjab were **typically lower **than in some other regions, generally around **30% to 40%** of the produce.
 
• The Ryotwari system in Punjab contributed to agricultural expansion and productivity, particularly in the context of **Green Revolution initiatives in the 1960s and 1970s.**
